segments.original: The 1990s and part of the 2000s were a prosperous time for comedies. The '80s were also an important time for the genre, but the two following decades proved that audiences were increasingly hungry for comedies of all kinds, bringing new actors and directors to stardom and dominating box offices around the world.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: Experimentation was abundant, with filmmakers such as Quentin Tarantino (b. 1963), Lars Von Trier (b. 1956), Paul Thomas Anderson (b. 1970) and the Coen brothers pushing boundaries and exploring new visual and narrative approaches to storytelling. The enormous blockbusters that today arrive in the form of Marvel and DC movies were still many years away, leaving room for a variety of genres to flourish. It was in this environment that the romantic comedy gained ground.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: It probably started with When Harry Met Sally... (1989), whose success built momentum. Soon, similar films set out to prove that, no matter how bad things seemed for a character, there was always room for unexpected improvement. Joyful laughs and sentimental romance became a guilty pleasure for many.

segments.original: As the '90s drew to a close, romantic comedies were as good as gold. In 1998 and 1999, respectively, three of the twenty highest-grossing films were romantic comedies. segments.original: Following the mold of Porky's (1981), released 18 years earlier, American Pie (1999) hit theaters, dividing critics. The film was a box office hit, and without realizing it, directors Paul Weitz (b. 1965) and Chris Weitz (b. 1969) kicked off a wave of crude comedies aimed at teenage audiences, in which the premise of "losing one's virginity" was one of the main plot points.

segments.original: A 1940s-style romantic comedy with a modern twist, Pretty Woman was a refreshing antidote to the macho slugfest movies that dominated Hollywood output in the late 1980s. One of the highest-grossing films of the 1990s, it succeeded in making "date movies" popular again.
segments.text: A nineteen forties-style romantic comedy with a modern twist, Pretty Woman was a refreshing antidote to the macho slugfest movies that dominated Hollywood output in the late nineteen eighties. One of the highest-grossing films of the nineteen nineties, it succeeded in making "date movies" popular again.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: The film also gave huge boosts to the careers of its stars, Richard Gere (who had not had a hit film since the mid-1980s) and Julia Roberts, who was nominated for an Oscar for her performance. Gere makes a fine gentleman as Edward Lewis, a powerful businessman on a trip to Los Angeles who ends up getting lost around Hollywood Boulevard and asks the hooker-with-a-heart-of-gold Vivian (Roberts in a tiny miniskirt and thigh-high boots) how to get to the Beverly Hills hotel. Being a smart and sensitive prostitute, Vivian offers to take him where he needs to go and, with her charm, soon gets him to hire her for a week as his "all-occasion" woman. As a reward for her time and effort, she gets unlimited access to his credit card to buy clothes and learns how to behave in a fancy restaurant (thanks to the hotel's friendly manager, played by Héctor Elizondo). And, unsurprisingly, Vivian falls in love with her benefactor.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: The whole story is highly improbable, of course. For starters, hardly any prostitute on Hollywood Boulevard is as well groomed as Vivian. Roberts's success in the role of a prostitute is politically incorrect, but the sheer charm of Pretty Woman never fails to shine through.

segments.speaker: narrador
segments.original: It was not only romantic comedies and gross-out comedies that stood out during these two decades. In the '90s, Jim Carrey (b. 1962), with his eccentric style, starred in Ace Ventura: Pet Detective (1994), The Mask (1994) and Dumb and Dumber (1994), all in the same year. The films were hits, making Jim Carrey one of the biggest names in the genre at the time. Eddie Murphy (b. 1961) followed the same path. Murphy had already been a household name since the 1980s, with the release of Beverly Hills Cop (1984). But it was with The Nutty Professor (1996) that we discovered Murphy's acting talent: he plays every member of Professor Sherman Klump's family.

segments.original: In the '80s, ZAZ-style comedy had dominated the box office with Airplane! (1980) and The Naked Gun: From the Files of Police Squad! (1988), but it ended up going on hiatus during the 1990s. Then, in 2000, the Wayans brothers released Scary Movie (2000). The film, which focused on poking fun at the major horror films released in the preceding years, was a tremendous success, reviving the parody subgenre. Films such as Epic Movie (2007), Meet the Spartans (2008), Superhero Movie (2008) and Tropic Thunder (2008) followed this line of humor.
